item.title: Four decades of citizen science reveal widespread declines in native plant distributions in Japan
item.description: [Ecology & Conservation] Keyword: citizen science — A new study led by researchers at Kyushu University has found that nearly 45% of 1,864 native plant species surveyed across Kanagawa Prefecture, Japan, were recorded in fewer locations over approximately four decades. item.title: Earth's next ice age may have already begun. Global warming stopped it
item.description: [Climate & Environment] Keyword: global warming — Scientists have uncovered surprising evidence that Earth’s next ice age may have already begun, only to be stopped by global warming. By studying ancient plants preserved beneath the Barnes Ice Cap in the Canadian Arctic, researchers discovered that the remnants of a massive ice sheet began expanding again about 2,000 years ago, signaling the possible start of a new glacial period. But by the 1960s, rising temperatures had reversed that growth, causing the ice to shrink instead.

item.title: Depression may be an early warning sign of Alzheimer's disease
item.description: [AI & Automation] Keyword: LLM — Depression in older adults may be more than a mental health concern. Scientists discovered that accumulating tau protein, a hallmark of Alzheimer's disease, was linked to worsening depressive symptoms in people who still had normal memory and thinking abilities. The faster tau built up in the brain, the faster depressive symptoms increased, suggesting that mood changes could emerge before cognitive decline.
